message.reasoning:
I need to make a decision in this Monopoly turn.

I'm at the JAIL space but not actually in jail. I have $86 cash and two properties with 2 houses each. Connecticut Avenue is mortgaged. This is the post-turn action phase after building.

Virginia Avenue has 3 houses. St. James Place, B&O Railroad, and Pennsylvania Avenue are mortgaged.

Claude has $195 and a dark blue monopoly with two houses on each property. He owns three unmortgaged railroads and mortgaged utilities.

GPT has $53 and is in jail with a red monopoly and light blue properties. Tennessee is mortgaged.

Gemini has $1081 and is in jail with no monopolies. He holds a get-out-of-jail card and owns Mediterranean, New York, Ventnor, and North Carolina.

Atlantic, Marvin Gardens, and Pacific are unowned.

I will end the turn unless a clearly favorable cash trade appears. $86 is still weaker than three railroads, one house on Illinois, or any dark blue property.

Unmortgaging Connecticut Avenue would cost $66, leaving only $20. Keeping it mortgaged is preferable because cash is more useful than a property that does not complete a monopoly. Virginia Avenue is the only sellable building space.

Selling a house on Virginia Avenue would bring cash to $136 but drop rent from $500 to $150. That is too steep. I will not trade unless forced. The pink monopoly is the main win path. Players in jail will likely land on those spaces.

Players exiting jail roll dice to advance. A roll of 3 lands on St. Charles Place, 5 on States Avenue, and 6 on Virginia Avenue. This confirms the pink monopoly is a high-traffic target.

Standard Monopoly rent for three houses on Virginia Avenue is $600, not the $500 stated in the game state. This suggests a variant rule. I will trust the stated value.

I am weighing whether to sell a house on Virginia Avenue. A roll of three railroads would cost $100, and selling one house there would bring cash to $136. That is enough to survive the hit. The engine only lists Virginia as sellable, which is odd.

The engine likely limits house sales to the highest property first, which is why only Virginia is currently sellable. I am now exploring a trade with Gemini. He has $1081 and wants monopolies, but his yellows and greens are incomplete. Pacific is unowned, and he lacks a complete green set.

Gemini previously rejected a trade for $100 plus Pennsylvania Avenue because Pacific is unowned, so the green set would remain incomplete. I am now evaluating other offers. Mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue still cannot complete greens. St. James Place plus New York does not complete oranges since Tennessee belongs to GPT. The B&O Railroad has little value alone, and Connecticut Avenue is not a useful light blue addition for him.

I am now considering trading Connecticut Avenue to GPT. He has only $53 cash but needs that property to complete his light blue monopoly and build. That would create another rent threat, though he cannot pay much in return.

Breaking GPT's red monopoly would be ideal, but he owns one house on each red property. Trading those monopolies would require selling all buildings first, and the engine might reject such trades.

I will not offer GPT a property with houses because the trade schema is ambiguous and he only has $53. I should avoid giving Claude cash or the B&O Railroad, since that would raise his rent to $200. With only $86, I cannot buy unowned properties from the bank. I am still searching for any trade that improves my position.

I will end the turn. No trade is clearly favorable. Selling mortgaged Pennsylvania Avenue to Gemini would waste an action and give away a green blocker. I will not propose that.
